purpose: Adversarially audit only the frozen validated Codex result, waiver-aware comparison and synthesis plan without acquiring new research facts.
post_audit_holds: Claude and Grok absence remains visible and confidence remains medium.
Dataset-reference and produced-model ledger edges remain candidate and grant no ownership, release, deployment or cascade authority.
Training method, data rights, privacy, intellectual property, export, security, safety, cost, energy, jurisdiction and records profiles remain mandatory before operational adoption.
Evaluation and checkpoint selection remain separate from publication, registry promotion and deployment authority.
All implementation, benchmark, telemetry, lineage and environmental mappings remain release-pinned and loss-declaring.
NIST AI RMF 1.0 remains pinned while its announced revision is incomplete.
audit_findings: The aggregate boundary is coherent: it owns one execution history and typed assertions while external data, code, model, evaluation, registry, deployment and infrastructure masters retain their lifecycles.
The structure prevents experiment definition, run, stage, attempt, checkpoint, trained artifact, registry entry and deployment from collapsing into one identity.
Planned configuration, requested resources, observed allocation, measured use, cost, energy and carbon remain source-qualified rather than interchangeable values.
Reproducibility claims are bounded by release, platform, hardware, dependencies, environment and known nondeterminism rather than inferred from seeds alone.
Autonomous resource acquisition, protected-data or secret access, publication, deployment and destructive cleanup are explicitly prohibited without delegated authority.
No unresolved critical semantic conflict prevents reviewable-draft publication.
